chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: The Ziegfeld audition and the salary haggling
summary: Bubbles launches into a song before they can be directed; Ziegfeld offers $500, Nazarro asks $750 and Bubbles says $800, and Gene Buck is told to give them a contract.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So we go to the Follies to get this job and do the audition. I know all this about the Follies now, kind of show it is, the biggest show in the world and everything, but Buck, he doesn't know about bigness, he just knows he plays the piano and what time the show starts and what time it's over, that's all. So we go do the shows and we go to the audition and Nazarro introduced us to Gene Buck and Florence Ziegfeld and there's a baby grand piano over there, Buck goes over to the piano and starts noodling around on the piano and I walk around the room looking out the window on Broadway, saying to myself, 'Ziegfeld Follies -- the Ziegfeld Follies, how about that.' And by that time I walked back to the piano and I said to Buck, 'We're going to do so-and-so-and-so for

the first song in about this tempo "Bap-Bop-Beep-Beep-Beep-Bup-Beep -- about that tempo, I'll let you know what it is, okay?" Allright. Wait a couple of minutes. I pick my chance to catch them when they weren't talking. And I jumped onto this song -- I go, "Bang, hit it." He hits it and I did this song and "Wang" and they were surprised -- Nazarro and Ziegfeld and Gene Buck were surprised when we hit this number like we did and go through that song and get it over with and they didn't get a chance to say do such and such a song -- let Mr. so-an-so hear you sing so-and-so. No, didn't get a chance to do that. I did it on my own, did this song. And when we finished this song, he never said, do a dance or do another gag or do a gag or do nothing. I finished the song and they started talking and in about less than five minutes our manager hollered over, "Boys, Mr. Ziegfeld wants to give you boys -- he say he can only pay you $500 a week. " I heard him. I said, "What did you say?" He said, "Mr. Ziegfeld can only
afford to pay you boys $500 a week and I'm asking for seven -- no, $750." He's asking for $750, he is. Ziggie can only pay $500. Okay.

I said, 'Well, I never like to interfere with the business part, but if Mr. Ziegfeld can only pay five and you're asking for $750, I'll say $800, just like that. Did you hear what I said? I could have said thousand just as easy as I said eight. But I already heard what the show -- who wants to do the show, and what I'll do the show for and so-and-so-and-so. And it ain't no bargain at $500, I can make $500 any time from this guy I'm working for. See what I mean? So to me, I can just raise it another $50 anyway and it won't hurt me none. And still this guy will be selling me and this guy will be buying me -- selling and buying in that deal. If he wants to pay $500 and the other guy wants to sell for $750 and I don't go for either one of their salaries and outside I meet the price and neither one of them bought or

sold me, neither one. The man who is going to hire me is going to pay me more money than what he said and more money than what Nazarro said. See what I mean? So I got past that one and Nazarro turned around to Mr. Ziegfeld, God rest his soul, turned around and said, Gene Buck, give them a contract. Just like that. Give us a contract.
